JUDGMENT
The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.80,00,000/- for the death of Mr.Mallappa in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners' case are as under:
2. That on 05.06.2024 at about 7.00 p.m. deceased Mallappa was proceeding in a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-52/W-4269 from Nelamangala towards Basavanahalli, when he reached Opp. Ranganatha Bar, Nelamangala - Siddamma vs Sumuka Enterprises on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168997742/
2 Doddaballapura road, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru District, at that time, driver of the goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-41/D-3579 came from opposite direction from Basavanahalli towards Nelamangala Town, drove the same with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
Due to which, deceased sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
Thereafter, post mortem was conducted at Government Hospital, Nelamangala and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners.

Subsequently, the petitioners have spent Rs.2,00,000/-
towards transportation of dead body, funeral, obsequies ceremonies and other incidental expenses.

3. It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 39 years, working as a Machine Operator in SD Hollo blocks, Kannegowdanahalli, Kasaba Hobli,
Nelamangala Taluk and earning Rs.30,000/- per month and contributing entire income towards the welfare of the family.

Due to untimely death of the deceased, life of the petitioners became dark,
miserable and put to great financial hardship.
4. It is contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-41/D-3579.
In this regard, Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said vehicle in Crime No.247/2024.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.

5. In response to the notice, respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal, remained absent,
placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
6. In the written statement, the respondent No.2 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further, this respondent has admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-41/D-3579 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It is also contention of the respondent No.2 that, the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.
It is the defence of the respondent No.2 that, the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased himself.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and relationship between deceased with the petitioners.
Ultimately contended that the claim of the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.

7. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Sri.Mallappa died due to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident which was taken place on 05-06-2024 at about 7-00 p.m. opposite Ranganatha Bar, on Nelamangala - Doddaballapura road,
Basavanahalli, Nelamangala, Bengaluru Distgrict due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the TATA ACE goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-41/ D-3579 in Siddamma vs Sumuka Enterprises on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168997742/
3 an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that they are legal heirs and were depending upon the income of the deceased?
3) Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, at what rate and from whom?

8. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P25.
9. On the other hand, respondent No.2 has not led any rebuttal on its behalf.

10. Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on record.
11.

My findings to the above issues as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.

Issue No.2: In the Affirmative Issue No.3: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4: As per final order, for the following:
R E A S O N S ISSUE No.1:-
12.

It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-41/D-3579, the alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, Mallappa died in the said accident.
As such, the petitioners have filed this claim petition against the respondents.
13. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the deceased and not on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

14. On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, first of all, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against the driver of the offending vehicle in question.
15. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 by name Siddamma got examined as PW1.
In her examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.

4
The petitioner in support of her oral evidence has relied upon the police documents at Ex.
P1 to Ex
16. On going through the documents, Ex.P1- true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No.247/2024 of Nelamangala Traffic Police Station.

Ex.P2-true copy of the first information statement given by petitioner No.1, Ex.P3-spot mahazar, Ex.P4 & Ex.P5- true copies of seizure mahazar, Ex.P6-true copy of spot sketch, Ex.P7-true copy inquest report, Ex.
P8-true copy of P.M. report,
Ex.P9- Notice u/s 133 of IMV act, Ex.P10-reply to the notice u/s 133 of M.V. Act,

Ex.P11- true copy of IMV report,
Ex.P12-statement u/s 161, Ex.P13-Voluntary statement and Ex.P14- true copy of charge sheet.

17. On perusal of the police documents it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by the petitioner No.1, the S.H.O. of Nelamangala P.S. have registered the case against the driver of Tata ACE goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-41-D-3579 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 304(A) of IPC.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against driver of the Tata ACE vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 & 304(A) of IPC.
18.

On the other hand, though the respondent No.2 has taken contention that the accident was not occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the TATA ACE vehicle, but not made an effort to examine either the driver of the offending vehicle or any of the independent eye witness to prove its contention.
19.
PW1 was subjected for cross-examination, but no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondents about the denial of allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle.
20. In the light of the evidence placed by petitioners, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the TATA ACE goods vehicle bearing No.KA-41-D-3579 and in the said accident, Mallappa succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2 to 4:
21.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P15 to Ex.P15 i.e., Aadhar cards of petitioners,
school certificate of petitioner No.2 and PAN cards of deceased, petitioner No.1, 5 & 6 have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.

sentences.text: Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the particulars of the petitioners mentioned in the cause title of the petition reflected that, the petitioner No.1 being the wife has lost her husband and the petitioner No.2 to 4 are children of the deceased have lost their love and affection of their father, petitioner No.5 & 6 are the parents of deceased, who lost their son in their old age, who was the backbone of the family.
Hence, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were dependents on the deceased during his lifetime.
23. The petitioners herein, have placed Aadhar card, which is marked at Ex.P15 to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
On going through the said document, the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 1.1.1984.
The accident occurred on 5.6.2024.

Therefore,
as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 40 years.

For his age, multiplier '15' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma"
Case.
24.
In connection with the work of the deceased, in the main petition and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was working as machine operator and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
The petitioners have not placed any documents to show the income of the deceased.
Hence, in the absence of the definite income of the deceased, it is opt to consider the notional income as per law
. It is pertinent to note that, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2024.

By keeping in mind about the year of the accident and also notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- for the year 2024.
25.

Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Honourable Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others, " It was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.

entities.text: 2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

26. Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3 rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4 th where the number of Siddamma vs Sumuka Enterprises on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168997742/
6 dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
27. In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, there are six persons were depending upon the income of the deceased.
Hence, as per the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14, 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.
28. In the present case, deceased was aged about 40 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "15" is applicable.

And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments, it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
As such, deceased was come under the purview of 40-50 years, 25% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- per month.
Annual income of the deceased was Rs.1,98,000/- per year.
Along with this, the future prospects of 25% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased comes to (Rs.1,98,000+49,500) = Rs.2,47,500/-.
And 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.

Thus, net loss of income comes to Rs.1,85,625/-
(Rs.2,47,500-Rs.61,875).

This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "15" which comes to Rs.27,84,375/-.
29.

Apart from this aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium and with respect to the funeral expenses to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following authority;
2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited.
V/ s Pranay Sethi and others, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

30. By relying upon the above said decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the amount of Rs.16,500/- is awarded under the head loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards funeral expenses and also by placing reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited v/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Others, the amount of Rs.44,000/- each is awarded to the petitioner No.1 to 6 under the head loss of consortium.

LIABILITY:
33.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Tata ACE goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA- 41-D-3579, alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioners in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the R.C.
owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
34. As per records insurance policy was valid from 14.10.2023 to 13.10.2024.
The alleged accident had taken place on 5.6.2024.
As such, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Hence, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 & 3 in the Affirmative and the issue No.3 is Partly Affirmative.

ISSUE No.4:
35.

In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following;
 O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

8
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.30,81,375/- (Rupees thirty lakhs eighty one thousand three hundred and seventy five only) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for the share of 45%, the petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled the share of 15% each and the petitioner No. 5 & 6 are entitled the share of 5% each.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.1, 40% of their share shall be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% of their share shall be released in favour of them through due process of law.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.2, to 4, being minors, entire amount shall be deposited in any Nationalised/Scheduled bank till they attain age of majority.
After attaining the age of majority, entire amount shall be released to them through due process of law.
The guardian of the petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
After deposit of compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.5 & 6, by considering the age of the petitioners, entire amount shall be released to them through due process of law.
[ Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
